  CITY COUNCIL

Tuesday, July 20, 2021  5:00 PM  Teleconference

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor has called a Special Meeting of the City Council, to be called to
order via teleconference at 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, July 20, 2021. The agenda for the Special Meeting with the
items of business to be transacted or discussed is set forth below.

Posted by the office of the City Clerk at 4:00 p.m. on Monday, July 19, 2021.

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 810 1440 4291 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 810 1440 4291, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

minutes_text:
MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 20, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A Special meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 5:02 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton

4.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  DISCUSSION ON POTENTIAL APPEAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION APPROVAL
  OF PA-210169

City Attorney Davis explained that this item has been agendized for procedural purposes due
to the 20-day appeal period within the City’s municipal code following all Planning Commission
actions. Since the July 13 City Council meeting was canceled, the next Regular City Council
meeting on July 27 would be outside of the 20-day appeal period. He further explained that if
any Council Member makes a motion to appeal this item, three votes in favor would be required
in order to initiate a Council appeal.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF outlined the concerns residents have expressed to her regarding
this project, such as neighborhood compatibility and “mansionization” of the City, as well as the
timing of this item being heard by the Planning Commission immediately following a holiday
weekend. She further explained that residents were concerned that Casaba Road homes were
used for the neighborhood compatibility study, and that no Commissioners were able to go
inside the neighboring home to see the view impacts from the new project.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF made a motion for:

  THE CITY COUNCIL TO INITIATE AN  APPEAL  OF  PLANNING
  COMMISSION APPROVAL OF PA-210169.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ asked staff if the property was flagged and noticed in
accordance with the City’s code requirements. Community Development & Public Works
Director Wahba confirmed the property was properly flagged and noticed as required, and
confirmed that Commissioners did visit the property. He also noted that this item was
originally noticed for the June Planning Commission meeting, then continued to a date
certain on July 6 allowing for more time.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated that the neighboring resident confirmed that no
Commissioners visited inside their residence in order to see the view impacts. She also
noted complaints that the staff report was published the Friday before a holiday weekend.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JULY 20, 2021
 MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that this decision was 7-0 in favor by the Planning
Commission, and that any resident who wishes to appeal this decision may do so through
the City’s established appeal process. He further explained that unless there was a policy
issue within this process, there is no reason for the Council to initiate an appeal when the
concerned parties may appeal the project themselves.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF clarified that the two primary policy concerns of the residents
were the Casaba Road homes being used to evaluate neighborhood compatibility rather
than homes from the Montecillo area, and the fact that no Commissioners went inside
neighboring resident’s homes to see the view impacts.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA confirmed with the City Attorney that the time for any resident
to appeal this project has not expired.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public testimony was received by neighbor Leah Robertson residing at 27121 Palos Verdes
Drive East, expressing her concerns about this project and the effects on her residence.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN confirmed that Ms. Robertson attended the Planning Commission
hearing. He also noted that he hesitates to disempower the Planning Commission without a
compelling reason, since the Planning Commission voted 7-0 in favor of this project. He
acknowledged the timing challenges following a holiday weekend, and also acknowledged the
immense amount of work put in by the Commission and staff on this project.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN seconded COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF’s motion.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ emphasized that there are procedures in place to allow
residents to appeal, and that the appeal window is still open. Discussion ensued regarding the
fees associated with appeals, the appeals process in place allowing for fairness for all
residents, as well as the significant amount of work required by staff for each project that goes
before the Planning Commission.

Resident Leah Robertson spoke once more regarding her concerns.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN asked for a roll call vote:

  AYES:  Huff
  NOES:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

The motion fails (1-4).

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN reiterated that the appeal period for residents is still open, and
that he voted against because the City’s policies and procedures were followed, He stated he
would be open to hearing any appeal brought forward by residents to the Council. He also
commended the hard work of the Planning Commissioners.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ echoed MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN’s comments
regarding the Planning Commission and expressed her support and appreciation for staff’s
hard work, ethics and integrity.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA echoed MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN’s statement
regarding openness to hearing the project anew if brought to the Council through the appeal
process.

5.  ADJOURNMENT

At 5:51 P.M. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the next Regular
City Council meeting to be held on Tuesday, July 27, 2021 at 7:30 p.m. via teleconference.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JULY 20, 2021

Lauren Pettit  Steve Zuckerman
